/**
 * GROQ: Structured Summary (JSON)
 * Tuned for Llama 3.3 to ensure valid JSON output
 */
export const GROQ_SUMMARY_JSON_PROMPT = `You are a silent meeting summarizer. Convert this conversation into concise internal meeting notes.

Output a JSON object with EXACTLY these four keys, using these exact names:
- "summary" (string): one-paragraph overview
- "keyPoints" (array of strings): bullet list of key points
- "actionItems" (array of strings): owner-prefixed action items, e.g. "Bob: Draft invite copy by Wednesday"
- "decisions" (array of strings): explicit decisions made

Do NOT use "overview", "highlights", or any synonym for these keys. The four keys above are required and must be present even if empty arrays.

RULES:
- Do NOT invent information.
- Sound like a senior PM's internal notes.
- Calm, neutral, professional.
- Output ONLY the JSON object. No prose, no markdown fences.

Response Format (JSON ONLY):
{
  "summary": "one-paragraph overview",
  "keyPoints": ["3-6 specific bullets"],
  "actionItems": ["Owner: specific next step", "..."],
  "decisions": ["explicit decision 1", "..."]
}
`;

// FOLLOW-UP EMAIL PROMPTS

66	export const TINY_CODE_HINT_PROMPT = `${TINY_CORE}
67	
68	MODE: Code hint. The user has shared a coding problem (screenshot or text). Output:
69	1. One first-person sentence stating the approach.
70	2. Full working code in a fenced block with language tag.
71	3. One first-person sentence dry-running a small input.
72	4. Time and space complexity, one bullet each.`;
73	
74	export const TINY_TITLE_PROMPT = `Generate a concise 3-6 word title for this meeting context. Plain text only. No quotes, no punctuation at the end.`;
75	
76	export const TINY_SUMMARY_JSON_PROMPT = `Convert this conversation into concise meeting notes. Return ONLY valid JSON with this shape:
77	{"summary": string, "keyPoints": string[], "actionItems": string[], "decisions": string[]}
78	No markdown, no commentary. JSON only.`;
79	
80	export const TINY_FOLLOWUP_EMAIL_PROMPT = `Write a short professional follow-up email after a meeting. 3-5 sentences. Friendly, specific, no fluff. Output the email body only — no subject line, no signature.`;
81	
82	export const TINY_MODE_GENERAL_PROMPT = `${TINY_CORE}
83	
84	ACTIVE MODE: General conversation. Adapt tone to context. Default to direct, helpful, first-person responses speakable in 30 seconds.
85	
86	Coding question (writing code is requested):
87	- Sentence 1 (one short sentence): your approach in plain English. Example: "I'll use a hash map to track seen values for O(n) lookup."
88	- Code: full working solution in a fenced markdown block with language tag (\`\`\`python, \`\`\`ts, etc.). No partial code.
89	- Sentence after the code (one short sentence): a dry-run on a small example. Example: "For [3,2,4] target=6, we see 3, then 2, then 4 → match with 2, return [1,2]."
90	- Final line: "Time: O(?) | Space: O(?)" with the actual complexities.
91	
92	ALL FOUR PARTS are required for coding answers. Do not output just code.`;
93	
94	export const TINY_MODE_LOOKING_FOR_WORK_PROMPT = `${TINY_CORE}
95	
96	ACTIVE MODE: Job interview. The user is the candidate. Use the provided resume and job description silently — speak as the candidate.
97	- Behavioral question: STAR pattern, 3-4 sentences, specific company/project.
98	- "Why this role / why us": bridge resume strengths to the JD requirements in 2-3 sentences.
99	- Technical question: precise answer first, then one sentence of justification.
100	
101	Specifics: Use details from the user's profile context if provided in the user message. Do NOT invent company names, dollar amounts, percentages, or specific metrics. If no profile context is given, speak in plausible general terms ("at my last role", "a key project") without fabricating numbers.`;
102	
103	export const TINY_MODE_SALES_PROMPT = `${TINY_CORE}
104	
105	ACTIVE MODE: Sales call. The user is the seller. Speak as them.
106	- Objection: acknowledge briefly, reframe with value, end with a forward question. 2-3 sentences.
107	- Discovery: ask one sharp open-ended question about their pain or goal.
108	- Pitch moment: one outcome-focused sentence + one specific proof point.
109	Never use coaching labels. Output only what the user says aloud.`;
110	
111	export const TINY_MODE_RECRUITING_PROMPT = `${TINY_CORE}
112	
113	ROLE OVERRIDE: This mode supersedes the "you ARE the user" rule above. You speak ABOUT the candidate to the user (the recruiter). Output observations and suggested probing questions, never first-person answers. Never role-play as the candidate. Never address the candidate directly.
114	
115	OUTPUT SHAPES:
116	- Observation + probe: a 1-2 sentence observation about the candidate's response, followed by ONE specific probing question the recruiter should ask. Example: "They explained the architecture in 'we' terms with no individual ownership signal. Probe: 'What part of the design did you personally drive end-to-end?'"
117	- Hire signal call: when the user explicitly asks for a hire signal, output the structured form: "**Hire signal:** [Lean Yes / Lean No / Strong Yes / Strong No]. <one sentence on best evidence>. <one sentence on biggest gap>."
118	
119	NEVER output answers in first person. NEVER say "I want you to..." or "Let me explain...".`;
120	
121	export const TINY_MODE_TEAM_MEET_PROMPT = `${TINY_CORE}
122	
123	ACTIVE MODE: Team meeting. The user is a participant. Speak as them.
124	- Status updates: one sentence on progress, one on blockers, one on next step.
125	- Decisions: state position, then one-sentence rationale.
126	- Disagreements: acknowledge the other view in one phrase, then counter with evidence.
127	
128	CAPTURE FORMAT — mandatory whenever the input contains a meeting/transcript turn (any line tagged [MEETING ...], [ENG ...], [PM ...], [STANDUP ...], or any speaker label conveying assignments, decisions, or risks). Output ONLY the capture lines — no prose preamble, no first-person commentary:
129	- Action items → 📋 [Who] to [What] by [When]
130	- Decisions → ✅ [Decision]
131	- Risks/blockers → ⚠️ [Risk + impact]
132	NEVER use prose narrative for action items. NEVER use bullets without emojis. Each item on its own line.
133	
134	Status request (the user is explicitly asked "what's the status on X?" or [MANAGER ...] asks for a status) is the ONLY exception — answer in first-person prose, not capture format.`;

content.thinking: Nothing filters action items; the prompts themselves lead the model to drop undated tasks. I'm rewording the recap prompts in MeetingPersistence.ts and the Groq prompt next.

input.old_string: - You MAY infer implied action items or next steps if they are logical consequences of the discussion
input.new_string:

content.text:
I fixed it. Nothing in the code was filtering those tasks out. The problem was the prompts that write the recap: none of them said undated tasks count, and the Groq prompt's only example was "Bob: Draft invite copy by Wednesday". That taught the model an action item needs a date, so "Priya will send the contract" got dropped.

What I changed:

- **`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`**: this builds the recap when you end a meeting. I added a rule to the shared rules block, so it applies to both the generic recap and the mode-specific section recaps. It says any task with a person on it is an action item, gives the Priya contract line as the example, and says never to drop an item for having no date or to make one up. I also reworded the `actionItems` field to "Owner: task, with the due date if one was given, otherwise '(no date given)'".
- **`electron/llm/prompts.ts`** (`GROQ_SUMMARY_JSON_PROMPT`): I added an undated example next to the Bob one and the same "include every owned task" rule. This prompt matters most, because the recap uses it whenever Groq is the model that answers.
- **`electron/llm/tinyPrompts.ts`**: I made the same fix in the small-model recap prompt. I also changed the live Team Meet "📋 [Who] to [What] by [When]" format so it writes "no date given" instead of skipping the item.

Undated items will now show up as something like "Priya: Send the contract (no date given)".

I haven't type-checked or tested this against a real model. These are only prompt text changes, so the way to confirm it is to record a short meeting where someone says "X will do Y" with no date, end it, and check the action items.
